name: pediatric orthopedics overview
title: Pediatric orthopedics: an injury (fracture pattern, growth plate, apophysis) or a developmental problem (hip dysplasia, clubfoot, leg shape, scoliosis); each column gives presentation, exam and x-ray, and treatment

root.title: A child's bone or joint problem: an INJURY, or a DEVELOPMENTAL problem?
lines: children's bone is porous and pliable, the periosteum thick, and the growth plate (physis) the weak point: a child FRACTURES where an adult sprains

groups.title: INJURY
lines: falls from low heights · sport · pedestrian struck · infant or toddler: NON-ACCIDENTAL injury

groups.title: DEVELOPMENTAL
lines: screen, then treat early; do not overtreat normal variants

head: h
Fractures of pliable bone
buckle · greenstick · plastic deformation
pres: less ligament injury or dislocation than adults

head: h
Growth plate: Salter-Harris
risk: growth ARREST → leg length or angular deformity
pres: sprains are rare in kids: think Salter-Harris I
inv: often missed; found late as growth arrest
tx: EVERY growth plate injury is serious

head: h
Apophysis
tendon insertion: pulled by fast growth + tight muscle
tx: • apophysitis: rest, ice, compression, elevation; activity as tolerated; anti-inflammatories as needed

head: h
Developmental dysplasia of the hip
shallow acetabulum → subluxation or dislocation
inv: • Barlow: hip slips OUT (adduct, push back)
• Ortolani: hip slips back IN (abduct, lift)

head: h
Clubfoot
ankle plantarflexed · heel and forefoot in varus
inv: progressive deformity and stiffness; walking and footwear suffer
tx: full time 3 months, then nights 2-3 years

head: h
Leg shape
in-toeing · out-toeing · bow legs · knock knees
h
Scoliosis
lateral curve + rotation · idiopathic: adolescent, F > M
inv: • rib prominence on the convex side
• full neuro exam, skin over the spine
tx: to STOP progression · by curve size and risk

panels.title: Pediatric elbow
items: ossification centres appear in order CRITOE at about 1 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 9 · 11 years: capitellum, radial head, internal (medial) epicondyle, trochlea, olecranon, external (lateral) epicondyle
swelling = suspect a bony injury · call pediatric orthopedics for a very swollen elbow, instability, a displaced fracture or an incongruously reduced dislocation

panels.title: A limping child
items: causes differ by AGE: missed hip dysplasia · clubfoot · hip disease (transient synovitis, Perthes, slipped capital femoral epiphysis) · overuse · trauma, accidental or not
warning signs in any abnormal gait: asymmetry · progressive · leg length difference · pain · deformity
see the CHILD WITH A LIMP chart
